Mosaic

moh-ZAY-ik — stress on second syllable · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A mosaic is a picture or design created by fitting together many small pieces of colored stone, glass, or tile.

The courtyard floor was a mosaic of tiny blue and gold tiles forming a peacock.

Worked Example

An artist collects fragments of broken pottery and colored glass from a demolished building. She carefully arranges them in a frame, fitting each piece snugly against the next until the fragments transform into a striking image of a flying bird.

Mosaic is precise here because it emphasizes not just that there is a picture or design, but specifically that it is made by fitting together many small, distinct pieces. Simply saying "picture" or "design" would miss the crucial element of assembly from fragments.

How Mosaic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

picture

picture: an image made to be viewed

collage

collage: artwork assembled from pasted-together pieces

composition

composition: an arrangement of parts into a whole

Antonyms

monolith

monolith: a single, massive, undivided block

uniformity

uniformity: total sameness, with no variety of parts

How Strong Is It? — fragment → arrangement → collage → mosaic

fragment vs. mosaic

fragment vs. mosaic: A fragment is just one broken piece — the smallest unit, far below a mosaic, which unites thousands of such pieces into a single picture.

arrangement vs. mosaic

arrangement vs. mosaic: An arrangement is any orderly grouping, but a mosaic is a precise, artistic arrangement in which every small tile locks into a larger design.

collage vs. mosaic

collage vs. mosaic: A collage is pieces pasted together loosely, while a mosaic is the most exacting version: small hard tiles fitted tightly together to form one polished image.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — mosa (musa)

Root — mosa (musa): of the Muses, the Greek goddesses of the arts (Medieval Latin (from Greek Mousa))

Put it together

Put it together: The root traces to the Muses, the Greek goddesses of art and inspiration: a mosaic was 'work worthy of the Muses' — an artwork painstakingly assembled from many small colored pieces of stone, glass, or tile.

Use the root in a new word: museum

Use the root in a new word: museum: A museum was originally a 'home of the Muses,' the Greek goddesses of the arts — and a mosaic was artwork fine enough to honor those same Muses.
